Fact.Name: Form 1099-DIV reports
Fact.Description: One item per Form 1099-DIV.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-DIV section is done
Fact.Description: The user has clicked "Done" for their Forms 1099-DIV.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-DIV recipient
Fact.Description: The filer who received the dividends on this form.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-DIV belongs to the secondary filer
Spouse's Form 1099-DIV on a return that is not joint
Any spouse's Form 1099-DIV on a return that is not joint
Fact.Description: Only a joint return includes the spouse's income (26 U.S.C. 6013(d)(3): on a joint return "the tax shall be computed on the aggregate income").

Fact.Name: Form 1099-DIV payer
Fact.Description: Payer's name. Also the Schedule B (Form 1040) Part II line 5 payer name when Schedule B is required: Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) p. 2, Line 5: "List on line 5 each payer's name and the amount of ordinary dividends you received."

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 1a: total ordinary dividends
Fact.Description: Form 1099-DIV (Rev. December 2027) draft, Instructions for Recipient, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1099div--dft.pdf: "Box 1a. Shows total ordinary dividends that are taxable. Include this amount on the “Ordinary dividends” line of Form 1040 or 1040-SR." Gross income includes dividends: 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(7) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/61).

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 1a, whole dollars
Fact.Description: Box 1a rounded to whole dollars, the Schedule B (Form 1040) Part II line 5 amount for this payer. Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) p. 2, Line 5: "Report on line 5 all of your ordinary dividends. This amount should be shown in box 1a of your Forms 1099-DIV or substitute statements."

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 1b: qualified dividends (as entered)
Fact.Description: Box 1b on the 1099-DIV. Optional; left blank means $0. Use /dividendReports/*/qualifiedDividends downstream.

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 1b: qualified dividends
Fact.Description: Form 1099-DIV (Rev. December 2027) draft, Instructions for Recipient, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1099div--dft.pdf: "Box 1b. Shows the portion of the amount in box 1a that may be eligible for reduced capital gains rates." Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 25, Line 3a: "Generally, these dividends are shown in box 1b of Form(s) 1099-DIV." 26 U.S.C. 1(h)(11) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1).

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 2a: total capital gain distributions (as entered)
Fact.Description: Box 2a on the 1099-DIV. Optional; left blank means $0. Use /dividendReports/*/capitalGainDistributions downstream.

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 2a: total capital gain distributions
Fact.Description: Form 1099-DIV (Rev. December 2027) draft, Instructions for Recipient, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1099div--dft.pdf: "Box 2a. Shows total capital gain distributions from a regulated investment company (RIC) or real estate investment trust (REIT)." Not computed in this module: any amount stops the return (/flowKnockoutCapitalGainDistributions).

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 3: nondividend distributions (as entered)
Fact.Description: Box 3 on the 1099-DIV. Optional; left blank means $0. Use /dividendReports/*/nondividendDistributions downstream.

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 3: nondividend distributions
Fact.Description: Form 1099-DIV (Rev. December 2027) draft, Instructions for Recipient, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1099div--dft.pdf: "Box 3. Shows a return of capital. To the extent of your cost (or other basis) in the stock, the distribution reduces your basis and is not taxable. Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain." 26 U.S.C. 301(c)(2)-(3) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/301). Not income while it does not exceed basis; above basis stops the return (/flowKnockoutNondividendDistributionsOverBasis).

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 4: federal income tax withheld (as entered)
Fact.Description: Box 4 on the 1099-DIV. Optional; left blank means $0. Use /dividendReports/*/federalTaxWithheld downstream.

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 4: federal income tax withheld
Fact.Description: Form 1099-DIV (Rev. December 2027) draft, Instructions for Recipient, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1099div--dft.pdf: "Box 4. Shows backup withholding. ... Include this amount on your income tax return as tax withheld." Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 39, Line 25b: "If you received a 2025 Form 1099 showing federal income tax withheld on dividends ... include the amount withheld in the total on line 25b. This should be shown in box 4 of Form 1099". 26 U.S.C. 31(c) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/31): "Any credit allowed by subsection (a) for any amount withheld under section 3406 shall be allowed for the taxable year of the recipient of the income in which the income is received."

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 5: section 199A dividends (as entered)
Fact.Description: Box 5 on the 1099-DIV. Optional; left blank means $0. Use /dividendReports/*/section199ADividends downstream.

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 5: section 199A dividends
Fact.Description: Form 1099-DIV (Rev. December 2027) draft, Instructions for Recipient, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1099div--dft.pdf: "Box 5. Shows the portion of the amount in box 1a that may be eligible for the 20% qualified business income deduction under section 199A. See the instructions for Form 8995 and Form 8995-A." 26 U.S.C. 199A(b)(1)(B) and (e)(3) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A). The QBI deduction (Form 1040 line 13b, taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction) is not modeled ($0), so any amount stops the return (/flowKnockoutSection199ADividends).

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 7: foreign tax paid (as entered)
Fact.Description: Box 7 on the 1099-DIV. Optional; left blank means $0. Use /dividendReports/*/foreignTaxPaid downstream.

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV box 7: foreign tax paid
Fact.Description: Form 1099-DIV (Rev. December 2027) draft, Instructions for Recipient, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1099div--dft.pdf: "Box 7. Shows the foreign tax that you may be able to claim as a deduction or a credit on Form 1040 or 1040-SR." Any amount stops the return (/flowKnockoutDividendForeignTaxPaid).

Fact.Name: 1099-DIV has an amount in an unsupported box
Fact.Description: Yes if the form has an amount in box 2b, 2c, 2d, 2e, 2f, 6, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15 or 16, a country in box 8, or box 11 (FATCA) checked. Form 1099-DIV (Rev. December 2027) draft, Instructions for Recipient, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1099div--dft.pdf: box 2b "unrecaptured section 1250 gain", 2c "Section 1202 gain", 2d "Collectibles (28%) gain", 2e/2f section 897, box 6 "your share of expenses of a nonpublicly offered RIC ... This amount is included in box 1a", boxes 9-10 liquidation distributions, box 11 FATCA, box 12 exempt-interest dividends, box 13 specified private activity bond interest dividends, boxes 14-16 state tax withheld.

Fact.Name: Dividends received as a nominee
Fact.Description: Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 26, Line 3b: "You must fill in and attach Schedule B if the total is over $1,500 or you received, as a nominee, ordinary dividends that actually belong to someone else." Schedule B Part II nominee subtraction is not modeled here.

Fact.Name: Some box 1b dividends aren't qualified dividends
Fact.Description: Asked when box 1b is more than $0. Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 26, Line 3a, Exception: "Some dividends may be reported as qualified dividends in box 1b of Form 1099-DIV but aren’t qualified dividends. These include ... Dividends you received on any share of stock that you held for less than 61 days during the 121-day period that began 60 days before the ex-dividend date", the preferred stock 91/181-day rule, related-payment obligations (including short sales) and payments in lieu of dividends. 26 U.S.C. 1(h)(11)(B)(iii) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1).

Fact.Name: Box 3 is more than the basis of the shares
Fact.Description: Asked when box 3 is more than $0. 26 U.S.C. 301(c)(3)(A) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/301): the nondividend portion "to the extent that it exceeds the adjusted basis of the stock, shall be treated as gain from the sale or exchange of property." Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 26, Nondividend Distributions: "After you get back all of your cost (or other basis), you must report these distributions as capital gains on Form 8949."

Fact.Name: Box 1b or box 5 is larger than box 1a
Fact.Description: Box 1b and box 5 are each "the portion of the amount in box 1a" (Form 1099-DIV instructions for recipient), so neither can exceed box 1a.

Fact.Name: Has seen last available screen
Fact.Description: Whether the user has reached the last screen for this Form 1099-DIV.

Fact.Name: At least one Form 1099-DIV is incomplete
Total ordinary dividends (1099-DIV box 1a)
Fact.Description: Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 26, Line 3b: "Each payer should send you a Form 1099-DIV. Enter your total ordinary dividends on line 3b. This amount should be shown in box 1a of Form(s) 1099-DIV." Feeds income /ordinaryDividends.

Fact.Name: Total qualified dividends (1099-DIV box 1b)
Fact.Description: Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 25, Line 3a: "Enter your total qualified dividends on line 3a. Qualified dividends are also included in the ordinary dividend total required to be shown on line 3b. ... Generally, these dividends are shown in box 1b of Form(s) 1099-DIV." Feeds income /qualifiedDividends. Box 1b amounts that are not qualified (p. 26 Exception) stop the return (/flowKnockoutQualifiedDividendsHoldingPeriod).

Fact.Name: Total capital gain distributions (1099-DIV box 2a)
Fact.Description: Not on Form 1040 in this module; see /flowKnockoutCapitalGainDistributions.

Fact.Name: Total nondividend distributions (1099-DIV box 3)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 301(c)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/301): "That portion of the distribution which is not a dividend shall be applied against and reduce the adjusted basis of the stock." Not income; not on Form 1040.

Fact.Name: Total federal income tax withheld on 1099-DIV (box 4)
Fact.Description: Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 39, Line 25b (see /dividendReports/*/federalTaxWithheld). Feeds taxCalculations /form1099Withholding.

Fact.Name: Total section 199A dividends (1099-DIV box 5)
Fact.Description: See /flowKnockoutSection199ADividends.

Fact.Name: Total foreign tax paid on 1099-DIV (box 7)
Fact.Description: See /flowKnockoutDividendForeignTaxPaid.

Fact.Name: Knockout: 1099-DIV box this tool can't compute
Fact.Description: Yes to /dividendReports/*/hasUnsupportedBoxes. Boxes 2b-2d need the Schedule D Tax Worksheet or Form 8949/Schedule D (Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 31, Line 7a, Exception 1 requires that none of the forms "have an amount in box 2b (unrecaptured section 1250 gain), box 2c (section 1202 gain), or box 2d (collectibles (28%) gain)"), 2e/2f are section 897 amounts, box 6 needs the nonpublicly offered RIC expense treatment, boxes 9-10 are liquidation distributions (basis recovery), box 11 FATCA may require Form 8938, box 12 exempt-interest dividends belong on line 2a and box 13 on Form 6251, and boxes 14-16 are state withholding. None is modeled.

Fact.Name: Knockout: 1099-DIV box 2a capital gain distributions
Fact.Description: Box 2a goes to Schedule D line 13, or straight to Form 1040 line 7a under Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 31, Line 7a, Exception 1 ("You have no capital losses, and your only capital gains are capital gain distributions from Form(s) 1099-DIV, box 2a"), and is taxed through the QDCG worksheet line 3. Neither path is computed in this module, so any amount stops the return instead of being left off line 7.

Fact.Name: Knockout: 1099-DIV box 3 above basis
Fact.Description: Yes to /dividendReports/*/nondividendDistributionsExceedBasis. The excess is capital gain (26 U.S.C. 301(c)(3)(A), https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/301) reported on Form 8949 (Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 26, Nondividend Distributions); stock basis is not collected here. At or below basis box 3 is not income (301(c)(2)).

Fact.Name: Knockout: box 1b dividends that aren't qualified
Fact.Description: Yes to /dividendReports/*/qualifiedDividendsHoldingPeriodNotMet. Line 3a would have to be less than box 1b by the nonqualified part (Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 26, Line 3a Exception; 26 U.S.C. 1(h)(11)(B)(iii), https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1); the per-share holding-period split is not collected.

Fact.Name: Knockout: 1099-DIV box 5 section 199A dividends
Fact.Description: Qualified REIT dividends are part of the 26 U.S.C. 199A(b)(1)(B) combined QBI amount (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A), claimed on Form 8995 or 8995-A and Form 1040 line 13b. QBI is not modeled (taxCalculations /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction is $0), so any amount stops the return rather than dropping the deduction.

Fact.Name: Knockout: 1099-DIV box 7 foreign tax paid
Fact.Description: The foreign tax credit without Form 1116 (Schedule 3 line 1) needs the 26 U.S.C. 904(j) election (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/904): (j)(2) "(A) the entire amount of such individual’s gross income for the taxable year from sources without the United States consists of qualified passive income, (B) the amount of the creditable foreign taxes paid or accrued by the individual during the taxable year does not exceed $300 ($600 in the case of a joint return), and (C) such individual elects to have this subsection apply". Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 115, Schedule 3 Line 1, Exception: Form 1116 isn't needed if "All of your foreign source gross income was from interest and dividends and all of that income and the foreign tax paid on it were reported to you on Form 1099-INT, Form 1099-DIV, or Schedule K-3", "The total of your foreign taxes wasn't more than $300 (not more than $600 if married filing jointly)", the 16-day holding period, no Form 4563 / Puerto Rico exclusion, and the taxes were legally owed and paid to recognized countries; then "Enter on line 1 the smaller of (a) your total foreign taxes, or (b) the total of the amounts on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16, and Schedule 2, line 1a." Otherwise Form 1116. Schedule 3 line 1 is still a $0 placeholder (schedule3 /sched3Line1, also used by the CTC, CDCC and Form 6251 line 10 computations) and 1099-INT box 6 already stops the return (interest /flowKnockoutHasForeignTaxPaid), so any box 7 amount stops the return too rather than dropping the credit.

Fact.Name: Knockout: dividends received as a nominee
Fact.Description: Yes to /dividendReports/*/receivedAsNominee. Form 1040 instr. (2025) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf p. 26, Line 3b: Schedule B is required if "you received, as a nominee, ordinary dividends that actually belong to someone else"; the Schedule B Part II nominee subtraction is not modeled here.

Fact.Name: Knockout: 1099-DIV box 1b or 5 larger than box 1a
Fact.Description: Box 1b and box 5 are each "the portion of the amount in box 1a" (Form 1099-DIV instructions for recipient). A larger amount means the form was entered incorrectly; stop rather than compute lines 3a and 3b from it.
